svg.title: Speeding up and slowing down depend on two signs
svg.desc: An object speeds up when velocity and acceleration have the same sign and slows down when their signs differ. The rule follows from whether the magnitude |v| is moving away from or toward zero. Negative velocity does not mean slowing down. It means motion in the negative direction. If acceleration is also negative, the velocity becomes more negative and the speed increases. The table organizes all four sign combinations so you can reason rather than guess from the word "negative." Negative velocity does not mean slowing down. It means motion in the negative direction. If acceleration is also negative, the velocity becomes more negative and the speed increases. The table organizes all four sign combinations so you can reason rather than guess from the word "negative." An object speeds up when velocity and acceleration have the same sign and slows down when their signs differ. The rule follows from whether the magnitude |v| is moving away from or toward zero. Negative velocity does not mean slowing down. It means motion in the negative direction. If acceleration is also negative, the velocity becomes more negative and the speed increases. The table organizes all four sign combinations so you can reason rather than guess from the word "negative." Every relationship in speeding up and slowing down depend on two signs is identified with written labels plus distinct solid, dashed, dotted, double, marker, or pattern cues; color is never the only carrier of meaning. Caption: An object speeds up when velocity and acceleration have the same sign and slows down when their signs differ. The rule follows from whether the magnitude |v| is moving away from or toward zero.
